<entry id="Q02041">
<head-word>פְּרָת</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.)
<pos> pr. n.</pos>
<italic>P’rath</italic>, </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> the river 
<italic>Euphrates</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 16 פ' שפ̇ר̇ה ורבה וכ' it is named 
<italic>P’rath</italic> (the growing), for its waters grow and increase, until people pass it on ships; פ' שמימיו פרין ורבין וכ' P’rath, for its waters are fruitful (fructifying); פ' שמפ̇ר̇יד והולך עד שכלה במגריפה ‘Rashi’ (ed. שמפרש) it is named P’rath (v. פְּרַת), because it goes on dividing (branching off in channels), until it ends under the (digging) spade; Yalk. Deut. 801 כמגרפה (corr. acc.); Sifré Deut. 6 שמפרה והולך עד שכלה מגריפה לגרפי it goes on fructifying (irrigating), until the spade ceases to dig it; Yalk. Gen. 22 מפריס והולך עד שהוא כלה ופותחין וכ' goes on dividing, until it disappears, and they open it with the spade. Bekh. 55
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.—Denom. פְּרָתִי, 
<plural-form>pl. פְּרָתִים</plural-form>. Midr. Till. to Ps. CXXXVII שתו מים הפ' ומתים they drank Euphrates water and died; (Pesik. R. s. 28 מימי הפרת).</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>P’rath</italic>, name of certain districts or towns.</definition>
<notes> Yoma 10
<sup>a</sup> פ' דמישן (= רחנת עיר, Gen. X, 11): פ' דבורסיף (= כלח ib.); Kidd. 72
<sup>a</sup> (expl. חביל ימא) פ' דבורסי, v. בּוֹרְסִיף.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<italic>to divide, dismember</italic> (of the basilisk whose look is believed to cause a person’s limbs to fall apart, v.

<notes>, quot. s. v. נָשַׁל; cmp. יַפְרִישׁ Prov. XXIII, 32). Targ. Is. XIV, 29 מְפָרֵית (some ed. מַפְרִית

<italic>Pe</italic>.; h. text יפריש, v. supra.]</notes></sense>

<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to belittle, make light of</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Lam. R. to II, 10 הוון חמשא … ומְפָרְתִין ליה בנבוכדנצר וכ' (read: ביה; Ar. ופרטין) five kings were sitting and sneering at Nebuchadnezzar in the presence of Zedekiah; אף הוא מְפָרְתֵיה לנב' וכ' (Ar. פרטיה, Var. פדרת, corr. acc.) he, likewise, sneered &c.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>

<entry id="Q02054">
<head-word>פָּשׁוּט</head-word>
<head-word>פְּשׁוּטָה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (part. pass. of פָּשַׁט) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>straight, </italic>
<pgbrk id="pg1245" />
<italic>plain, simple</italic>.</definition>
<notes> R. Hash. III, 3 של יעל פ' a straight horn of the mountain-goat, opp. כפוף. Sabb. 104
<sup>a</sup>, v. כָּפַף. Ib. 106
<sup>a</sup>, v. סִיט. Men. 35
<sup>b</sup> ר' אחא מחוי פ' Ms. M. (ed. אשי) R. A. showed the index finger straight, i.e. the strap must reach from the arm to the tip of the index finger, when straightened, opp. כפוף (v. Tosaf. a. l.; Rashi: the strap must be as long as the distance from the thumb to the index finger, stretched as wide as possible, opp. כפוף the distance from the index to the middle finger). Mekh. B’shall. beg. לא הביאן הק"בה דרך פ' וכ' the Lord did not lead them on the direct road to Palestine; Yalk. Ex. 226 בפשוטה (sub. דרך). Mekh. l. c. לא הביאן המקום בפישוטן (corr. acc.). Cant. R. to I, 16 בלשון פ' with a single expression (of praise), opp. כפול. B. Bath. X, 1, a. fr. גט פ' a plain, open document, opp. מקושר folded; Tosef. Gitt. VIII (VI), 9 פ' ed. Zuck. (Var. גט פ'). Y. R. Hash. III, 58
<sup>d</sup> top פשוטה (sub. תקיעה) the plain note (תקיעה), opp. the tremulous note; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (noun) פָּשׁוּט 
<italic>the plain, literal sense</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. 63
<sup>a</sup>, a. e. אין מקרא יוצא מידי פְשׁוּטוֹ, v. מִקְרָא.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition> (sub. יורש) 
<italic>an heir entitled to a single share</italic>, opp. בְּכוֹר.</definition>
<notes> Bekh. 52
<sup>b</sup> מה חלק פ' ירושה וכ' as the share of the plain heir is an inheritance, so the share of the firstborn is an inheritance (and not a gift affected by the jubilee laws); B. Bath. 124
<sup>a</sup>. Ib. 126
<sup>a</sup> בכור … כפ' ויתר, v. וָתַר; Y. Keth. IV, end, 29
<sup>b</sup> בכור שחלק בפ' (read בפ'). Num. R. s. 6 בני פ' the sons of a plain (not firstborn) man; a. fr.—
<italic>Fem</italic>. פְּשׁוּטָה (sub. ירושה) 
<italic>single share</italic>. Y. B. Bath. VIII, 16
<sup>b</sup> top, opp. כְּפֵילָה.—
<plural-form>Pl. פְּשׁוּטִים, פְּשׁוּטִין; פְּשׁוּטוֹת</plural-form>. Sabb. 103
<sup>b</sup>, v. כָּפַף. Num. R. l. c. פְּשׁוּטֵי הלוים וכ' the plain (not firstborn) Levites took the place of the firstborn Israelites; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—4)</number>
<definition>
<italic>flat, level, without receptacle</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tosef. Kel. B. Bath. VI, 1 המשנה … מן הפ' לקיבול if one changes a leather implement … from a flat surface to a receptacle. Ib. IV, 3 פְּשׁוּטוֹ טהור in its flattened condition (when the bag is unrolled), it is not susceptible to uncleanness; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. as ab. Kel. II, 1 פְּשׁוּטֵיהֶן</plural-form> those of them which are flat, opp. מקבליהן which have receptacles. Sabb. 123
<sup>b</sup>, a. e. פְּשׁוּטֵי כלי עץ flat wooden implements (boards &c.). Y. ib. X, end, 12
<sup>d</sup> בפ' when they are flat, opp. מקופלין folded; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<notes> Sabb. I, 1, sq. פ' העני את ידו וכ' if the recipient puts his hand forth to within (the house). Pes. 118
<sup>b</sup>, a. e. שפּוֹשְׁטִין, v. פַּס II. Gen. R. s. 28 לא פָשְׁטוּ ידיהם במצות they (the Sodomites) never stretched their hands forth for good deeds (charity); Lam. R. to IV, 6; Yalk. Ez. 351. Ber. 3
<sup>b</sup>; Snh. 16
<sup>a</sup> לכו פִשְׁטוּ וכ', v. גְּדוּד. Men. I, 2 פושט את אצבעותיו וכ' he stretches his fingers so as to reach his wrist. Lev. R. s. 2 פושטין לו יד we must reach forth our hands to him, v. כָּנָף. <sup>b</sup> טליתו וכ' … ה' R. El. tied up his cloak and threw it over his back and went off; Tosef. ib. I, 9 … רגליו וכ' ה' (read בגדיו, v. infra) R. <senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to open, begin</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Ber. VI, end, 10
<sup>d</sup> על כל … שהיה פוֹתֵהַ וכ' over each cask as he opened it he said the benediction &c. Sabb. 104
<sup>a</sup>, a. e. פּוֹתְחִין לו (Var. פְּתָחִין), v. טָמֵא I. Ib. 48
<sup>a</sup> מתירין … אבל לא פותחין you may untie the neck-hole of a shirt, but not cut it open (on the Sabbath). Y. Taan. I, 64
<sup>b</sup> top (ref. to Is. XLV, 8) כנקבה … פוֹתַחַת וכ' like the female that opens for the male. Ned. III, 4 לא יִפְתַּח לו בנדר he must not begin (offer his willingness) to make a vow (in order to escape robbery &c., v. נָדַר); a. v. fr.—Part. pass. פָּתוּחַ; פְּתוּחָה; 
<plural-form>pl. פְּתוּחִים, פְּתוּחִין; פְּתוּחוֹת</plural-form>. Yeb. 71
<sup>b</sup>, a. e. נסתם הפ', v. סָתַם. Snh. 94
<sup>a</sup>, v. סָתַם (v. מנצפ"ך). Meg. 3
<sup>a</sup>, פ' באמצע, v. סָתַם. Erub. IV, 6 שלש חצירות הפ' זו לזו ופ' וכ' three courts opening into (communicating with) one another and into the publicroad; a. v. fr.—פתח פתוח, v. פֶּתַח.—Esp. (פרשה) פְּתוּחָה 
<italic>a paragraph in the Torah beginning with a new, indented line</italic>, opp. סתומה. Treat. Sof’rim I, 14 איזהו פ' כל שלא וכ' what is an open paragraph? Such as does not begin at the beginning of a line, וכמה … ותהא נקראת פ' and how much space must one leave … for a paragraph to be called open?; a. fr.—Trnsf. [
<italic>to open the door to</italic>,] 
<italic>to introduce</italic> (into learning). Y. M. Kat. III, 83
<sup>b</sup> top איזהו רבו כל שפ' לו תחלה who is called one’s (special) teacher? He who was the first to initiate him; a. e.—Esp. 
<italic>to open an opportunity for retracting a vow, to suggest reasons which, if known at the time, would have prevented the person from making the vow</italic>, v. חֲרָטָה. Ned. IX, 1 פותחין לאדם בכבוך וכ' the judges offer suggestions taken from the respect due to parents (saying, if you had known that this vow cast a reflection on your father &c.). Ib. רִפְתְּחוּ לו בכבוד המקום why not suggest to him the reverence due to the Lord (‘if you had known that he who makes a vow is considered an evil-doer &c.’)? Ib. 4 פותחין לו מן הכתוב וכ' we offer suggestions to him from what is written in the Law, saying to him, if you had known that (in fulfilling that vow) you would transgress the law forbidding revenge &c.; a. fr.—B. Kam. 27
<sup>a</sup> פ' בכד וסיים בחבית the Mishnah begins with 
<italic>kad</italic> and closes with 
<italic>ḥabith!</italic> Ber. 10
<sup>a</sup> פ' בה באשרי וכ', v. סוּם I h. Gen. R. s. 84 אתה פָתַחְתָּ תחלה בהצלת וכ' thou wast the first man to speak of saving life; אתה פתחת בתשובה וכ' thou wast the first to do repentance, … one of thy descendants shall rise and be the first (prophet) to call for repentance; a. fr.—Esp. 
<italic>to open a lecture with a</italic> (
<italic>Biblical</italic>) 
<italic>text</italic>. Pesik. Aḥăré, p. 170
<sup>a</sup> ר' לוי פ' וכ' R. Levi took up the text (Ps. LXXV, 5) &c. Gen. R. s. 1; a. v. fr.—Pesik. R. s. 33 [an editorial gloss] פ' בכל אלו הפרשיות the author takes his texts from all those (quoted) passages.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>

<italic>absence of virginity</italic> Keth. 9
<sup>b</sup> טענת פ' פ', contrad. to טענת דמים, v. דָּם. Ib.
